title: Throughput acceptance kit for Dedicated capacity: standardized harness, metrics and customer tests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: deliver a reproducible, audit-friendly acceptance kit that product, solutions, and SRE teams can use to validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior for customer signoffs. The kit includes a distributed load harness, canonical workload profiles (inference patterns, prompt mixes), a measurement methodology with SLO gates, and templated customer acceptance tests that can be run by engineering or shared with customers during onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness that can run locally and in CI (k8s Job) and produce an artifacts bundle (CSV + JSON + flamegraphs + consolidated logs).
Defined canonical workload profiles (low-latency chat, long-context generation, embedding batches) represented as templated request generators.
Measurement methodology doc that prescribes warmup, KV cache priming, steady window length, and metric aggregation rules used in acceptance decisions.
Automated gating: P95 latency, P99 latency, aggregate error rate, sustained throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), and scaling time windows evaluated against declared SLA thresholds.
Customer acceptance test templates that map customer SLAs to harness scenarios and provide step-by-step runbooks for validation and evidence collection.
End-to-end example run in staging with artifacts uploaded to the results S3 bucket and a sample customer signoff note.
Basic resilience checks: model-fallback during capacity pressure, per-tenant fairness under noisy neighbors, and rate limit enforcement behavior.
test_plan: Component tests: unit tests for workload generator templates, CI integration for artifact packaging.
Small-scale verification: run harness against single-pool Dedicated replica set (2-4 GPUs) to validate metrics plumbing and CSV/JSON outputs.
Scaling verification: progressive ramp from 10% to 100% of target throughput to validate autoscaling policy sensitivity and scaling latency.
Soak test: 24-hour steady-window run at 60% declared throughput to detect memory leaks, degradation, or gradual error increases.
Canary customer validation: run customer-specific workload profile with Solutions Engineer present and collect artifacts for signoff.
Failure injection: simulate node loss and network partition to confirm graceful degradation and fallback behavior while maintaining acceptance gates where possible.
measurement_methodology: Warmup: ignore first 120s of any run to allow kernel compilation, KV priming and cache stabilization.
Steady window: evaluate metrics over a minimum 10 minute contiguous steady window where throughput variance <= 5%.
Aggregation: use request-level timestamps to compute p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies for both token-level and response-level measurements; report mean and median throughput (tokens/sec and req/sec).
Error handling: classify client errors and server errors separately; acceptance fails if server error rate (5xx/500-like) exceeds 0.1% over steady window.

Autoscaling gates: record scale-up time (time to add capacity and restore target throughput) and scale-down time; scaling considered acceptable if 90% of scale-up events finish within configured scaling SLO (default 90s).
Noise isolation: run a 2nd concurrent noisy-tenant profile during one verification run to validate isolation and per-tenant QoS policies.
harness_components: Distributed coordinator (k8s Job + Redis lock) to orchestrate ramp phases across worker pods.
Workload generator templates: chat-streaming, batch-embed, long-context generation (with real-length distributions), and sampling temperature variations.
KV priming utility to pre-populate prefix caches at configurable hit rates.
Metric exporter that emits request traces, per-token timing, and custom histograms compatible with Prometheus + OpenTelemetry.
Artifact packager that zips logs, flamegraphs (perf/pprof), raw metrics, and a JSON summary for uploads to results store.
Runner shim to convert a harness run into a reproducible GitHub Actions job or a local docker-compose for quick debugging.
decisions: Adopt a single canonical steady-window definition (10 minutes) for acceptance to avoid fragile short-window artifacts.
Measure both token-level and response-level latencies; acceptance will use response-level p95/p99 but token-level used for optimization diagnostics.
Default autoscaling SLO: 90s for 90th percentile of scale-up events. This can be overridden per-customer SLA with explicit documentation.
Expose harness results in a standardized artifact bundle and require at least one staged customer run for any Dedicated plan that claims throughput guarantees.
next_steps: MVP implementation: deliver the coordinator, one workload (chat-streaming), and artifact packager — target end of cycle (2025-W09).
Draft the confluence runbook with CLI examples and a GitHub Actions template for CI-triggered acceptance runs.
Schedule cross-team review with PM (Lina Gomez) and Solutions Eng (Priya Sinha) to review customer test templates.
Create a small pilot with two existing Dedicated customers to validate the runbook and capture signoff artifacts.
